question: Under the current NTEP (National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme), drug-sensitive TB in children is treated with daily fixed-dose combinations (FDC) following a 2HRZE + 4HRE regimen, not the older thrice-weekly DOTS schedule.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. NTEP uses DAILY FDC dosing — the old RNTCP thrice-weekly intermittent regimen is obsolete. The regimen is 2HRZE + 4HRE with weight-band dosing. Always write NTEP (not RNTCP) and DAILY (not thrice-weekly) in examinations and clinical records.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. NTEP replaced RNTCP and mandates DAILY weight-band FDC dosing — 2 months intensive phase with Isoniazid + Rifampicin + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol (2HRZE), followed by 4 months continuation phase with Isoniazid + Rifampicin + Ethambutol (4HRE). Citing thrice-weekly dosing or RNTCP in examinations is a common and serious error.
